status: Completed author review of adult meropenem card and scored form.

sources.scope: Lists a 1-g meropenem vial. The registry does not establish current stock or formulation in IBD2.
Indications, reconstitution and administration, renal adjustment, hypersensitivity, seizures, C. difficile, decreased valproate and cell-wall mechanism.
Corroborates substantial serum valproate decrease in meropenem-exposed patients.

facts.sourceExcerpt: Carbapenem beta-lactam that binds penicillin-binding proteins and inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis.
facts.rationale: Connect PBP binding to cell-wall synthesis inhibition.

facts.sourceExcerpt: Serious susceptible bacterial infections. Current labeling includes complicated skin/skin-structure infection
facts.rationale: Choose a labeled complicated skin or soft-tissue treatment scenario.

facts.sourceExcerpt: it should not be treated as routine orthopaedic prophylaxis simply because it is broad spectrum.
facts.rationale: Choose procedure-specific prophylaxis without unnecessary carbapenem exposure.

facts.sourceExcerpt: IV. Reconstitution, dilution, infusion method and dose depend on the exact product, indication and renal function.
facts.rationale: Choose supplied product requirements and the verified infusion order. Indication is tested separately in the treatment question.

facts.sourceExcerpt: Current labeling requires dose adjustment when renal function is reduced.
facts.rationale: Identify that impaired clearance can require dose or interval adjustment.

facts.sourceExcerpt: Check beta-lactam allergy history and monitor for hypersensitivity.
facts.rationale: Identify relevant immediate carbapenem reaction and multisystem symptoms.

facts.sourceExcerpt: Review renal function because accumulation increases adverse-effect risk.
facts.rationale: Identify the renal basis of accumulation and regimen review.

facts.sourceExcerpt: Watch for seizures/neurologic changes, particularly with renal impairment
facts.rationale: Identify myoclonus and confusion in renal decline and escalate possible seizure risk.
Recognize pre-existing seizure disorder despite normal clearance.
Recognize significant watery diarrhea and cramping during antibiotic exposure.

facts.sourceExcerpt: meropenem can markedly lower valproic acid/divalproex concentrations and trigger breakthrough seizures.
facts.rationale: Identify the direction of the interaction and seizure consequence.

facts.sourceExcerpt: broad coverage does not replace culture-guided therapy and antimicrobial stewardship.
facts.rationale: Apply susceptibility and clinical response to reassess broader coverage.

facts.sourceExcerpt: WARD-OBSERVED repeatedly in IBD2 at Nasser Medical Complex in Oct 2026. Exact vial strength was not recorded; verify the vial and order.
facts.rationale: Dated ward observation, with no verified current product.

facts.sourceExcerpt: Broad-spectrum IV antibiotic for serious susceptible infection.
Renal adjustment + seizure risk; major interaction with valproic acid/divalproex.
